info.title: Relay X · Regulatory API
info.summary: The cosmetics regulatory corpus, read-only and bi-temporal.
info.description:
## In short

A **READ-ONLY** API over a cosmetics regulatory corpus: it serves data, it does not take
any in.

**Every response states what it does not cover**, so you never misread an empty result:

- `subscription`: the markets your plan does not cover;
- `withheldByScope`: the content your key is not allowed to redistribute;
- `absenceMeans` (in `/coverage`): what an absence of results lets you conclude.

⚠️ **Never read an empty list as "this substance is unregulated".**
Check the fields above first: they distinguish the possible causes of an empty result.

## Bi-temporality

The corpus carries two axes of time, and confusing them misdates a repeal:

- the time of the **LAW**: `validity`, and the `asOf` parameter that replays it;
- the time of **KNOWLEDGE**: `knowledge.knownFrom` / `knownUntil` / `isCurrent`,
  served by `/entries/{logicalEntryId}/history`, and `/changes` which builds on it.

`knownUntil: null` means "this is what we know TODAY", never
"date unknown".

## Value formats

To remove any ambiguity about the shape of fields, both on INPUT and OUTPUT:

- **Dates**: ISO 8601, `YYYY-MM-DD` (e.g. `2026-08-04`). Fields marked `format: date`.
- **Date-times**: ISO 8601 in UTC, `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ` (e.g. `2026-01-01T00:00:00Z`).
  Fields marked `format: date-time`. Always UTC (`Z`).
- **CAS number**: `NNNNNNN-NN-N` (2 to 7 digits, hyphen, 2 digits, hyphen, 1 check digit), e.g. `50-00-0`.
- **EC number** (EINECS/ELINCS): `NNN-NNN-N` (e.g. `200-001-8`).
- **CELEX** (`text.celexNumber`): EUR-Lex identifier, e.g. `32009R1223`.
- **`logicalEntryId`**: UUID v4, to be copied VERBATIM from a response, never composed by hand.
- **Territory codes**: `EU`, `GB`, `US`, `US-CA`, `CN`, `KR`, `JP`, `ASEAN`, `CA`, `BR`…
- **Numbers**: decimal point, never a thousands separator (e.g. `0.5`).

## Authentication

An API key, in the `X-Api-Key` header or as `Authorization: Bearer`. Keys are created
and revoked from the client console. The secret is shown ONLY once:
the database holds only a SHA-256 fingerprint of it.

## Parameters

A query parameter the endpoint does not read is not applied: the response then carries
`ignoredParameters` (see the `ParametresIgnores` schema). A read parameter passed MORE than once
is refused (`400 ambiguous_parameter`), except `sections`. Dates follow strict ISO 8601
(`YYYY-MM-DD`, or a date-time; without an offset it is read as UTC); any other form is
refused rather than reinterpreted.

## Quota

Per **SUBSCRIPTION** and per minute · **not per key**. All the live keys of one
subscription (up to 10) share a SINGLE ceiling: issuing more of them, or rotating a key,
does not raise the allowed throughput.

⚠️ Size your integration on that single ceiling. Spreading load over ten keys in the
belief that it multiplies throughput just drains the SAME window ten times faster.

Every response carries `RateLimit-Limit`, `RateLimit-Remaining`, `RateLimit-Reset` and
`RateLimit-Policy`, including those that succeed, because it is as you APPROACH the
ceiling that the information matters · those values describe the whole subscription, not
the key you presented. Going over returns 429 with `Retry-After`.

The window is FIXED: it opens on the first call, lasts 60 seconds and reopens in full at
`RateLimit-Reset`, which is a Unix timestamp in seconds. A scope refusal (403) carries
the window state without consuming a unit; a key refusal (401) carries none.

⚠️ A batch entry consumes one quota unit: a batch saves latency, not quota. The headers
of a batch response give the state AFTER every evaluated entry.

⚠️ MCP requests count against that same ceiling: HTTP and MCP do not get two windows.

get.summary: The constraints that apply to a substance, on a given date
get.description:
Returns the regulatory constraints that apply to a substance on a given date. Provide at least one identifier: `cas`, `ec`, `inci` or `name`.

⚠️ **An empty list does not mean "unregulated".** Also check `subscription` (the market may be outside your plan) and `withheldByScope` (the source text may not be redistributable under your key): both fields are present in every response.

⚠️ **A search by identifier does not reach GROUP entries** (for example "X and its salts"), which often carry no number. Search by `name` as well. The `searchMeans` field states what your search covered.

parameters.name: cas
parameters.description: CAS number, format `NNNNNNN-NN-N` (2 to 7 digits, hyphen, 2 digits, hyphen, 1 check digit), e.g. `50-00-0`. Matching is on a WHOLE token: `50-29-3` does not match `149850-29-3`.

parameters.name: ec
parameters.description: EC number (EINECS/ELINCS), format `NNN-NNN-N` (e.g. `200-001-8`).

parameters.name: inci
parameters.description: INCI name (the international nomenclature, the one on labels and raw-material sheets). ⚠️ The INCI index is PARTIAL and ENRICHED (never read from the law): it comes from CosIng (European Commission) and the Chinese IECIC inventory. A match goes first through this index, then, in OR, through literal names. A miss means "not in the index and no entry carries this string", never "this INCI is unrestricted".

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Literal name, searched as a WHOLE TERM across the three name fields of the entry · bounded by Unicode word boundaries, NOT as a substring. `SALICYL` finds nothing, `SALICYLIC ACID` finds. Non-Latin scripts (Chinese, Korean, Japanese) fall back to plain inclusion, for want of a word separator. Three characters minimum.

parameters.name: clpIndex
parameters.description: CLP index · the key of Table 3 of Annex VI to the CLP Regulation, format `NNN-NNN-NN-N`. The last position may be `X`. Hyphens are optional: `607746001` is accepted.

parameters.name: colourIndex
parameters.description: Colour index, format `CI NNNNN`. Every spelling is accepted: `CI77491`, `ci 77491`, `77491`.

parameters.name: synonym
parameters.description: Alternative designation carried by the substance index · trade name, common name, former nomenclature. EXACT match on the normalised form (case and spacing are ignored).

parameters.name: territory
parameters.description:
Territory code (`EU`, `GB`, `US`, `US-CA`, `CN`, `KR`, `JP`, `ASEAN`, `CA`, `BR`…). ⚠️ An UNKNOWN code returns `400` (`unknown_territory`, carrying the `knownTerritories` list), not an empty `200`: a misspelled code returning zero results would read as "no constraint on this market", the opposite of the truth. The real traps are `EU` versus `EC`, `CN` versus `NMPA`, `US` versus `USA`.

⚠️ **Behaviour change on 2026-08-11**: `/changes`, `/texts` and `/coverage` PREVIOUSLY returned `200` with zero rows on an unknown code. They now return `400`, as `/substances/lookup` already did. A client that treated that emptiness as a normal answer must handle the `400`.

⚠️ A VALID code outside your contracted zones raises NO error: it returns `200` with zero rows, and `subscription.missingZones` names the missing zone. The two kinds of emptiness are therefore never conflated.

parameters.name: territoryOnly
parameters.description:
Needs `territory`. By default a country returns EVERYTHING that applies there: its own rows, the rows of the union whose law applies directly (`FR` → `EU`) and the rows it borrows by regime reference (`CH` → EU annexes), each under its own code. `true` returns only the rows the territory prints ITSELF.

⚠️ Under `true`, an empty result does NOT mean "nothing applies": `territoryScope.excluded` names what was left out. Any value other than `true`/`false` returns `400 invalid_parameter`, never a silently widened read.

parameters.name: asOf
parameters.description: The LAW date to replay, in **ISO 8601 `YYYY-MM-DD`** format (e.g. `2026-08-04`). Defaults to today. ⚠️ Entries with no known start date appear applicable on ANY date: `asOf` is only a reliable replay of the law when the entry carries a start date.

parameters.name: sections
parameters.description: Restrict the response to the blocks you want, comma-separated. Aliases: `regulatory` (the constraints in force and upcoming), `toxicological` (scientific opinions and screening lists), `informative` (use precedents and procedures under way). Fine names also accepted: `constraints`, `opinions`, `screening`, `precedents`, `pipeline`. ⚠️ An unrequested block is ABSENT, not empty: its absence means nothing. Omit the parameter to get everything; when set, the response carries `sectionsReturned` and `sectionsMeans`.

parameters.name: lang
parameters.description: The language of the curated explanations (the `means` of screening lists and precedents). ⚠️ It has NO effect where an endpoint serves no explanation of those two families: on `/substances/impurity-limits` the response is byte-identical in `en` and in `fr` (measured 2026-08-26). Accepted there for call-site consistency, never as a promise. English by default. Also negotiable via the `x-app-locale` or `Accept-Language` header. French remains the authoritative version; English is a reviewed translation of it.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size. Capped at 200 server-side; a missing, null or uninterpretable value falls back to 50. No error is raised: the value is CLAMPED.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Pagination offset. Any non-positive value counts as 0, with no error. ⚠️ NO ceiling is enforced on this HTTP surface: an offset beyond `total` returns an empty page, it is never silently MOVED to another page. The MCP server, by contrast, clamps beyond a hard maximum and says so in `pagination.offsetClamped` · a pagination loop written for one does not transpose as is to the other.

parameters.name: view
parameters.description:
The VERBOSITY of each constraint served. Defaults to `full` on this route · the historical contract is unchanged and the trimming is OPT-IN.

· `full` · the whole constraint, as described by `Contrainte`.
· `standard` · the same, without the explanatory prose (every `means` key or key ending in `Means`, measured at 52 % of the payload) and without `literal.fullText`. No decision field is removed, but the `means` that `Contrainte` marks required are ABSENT.
· `summary` · a FLAT, strictly decisional object, described by `ContrainteResumee` · about 12 % of the payload. It is NOT a truncated `Contrainte`, it is a different shape.

⚠️ An unknown value raises NO error: it falls back to the default. No view removes or alters the coverage disclosures (`subscription`, `withheldByScope`, `identifierCaveats`), which guard against a misreading and are served identically.

The response then carries a `view` echo field · absent when the view is `full`.

parameters.name: context
parameters.description:
Whether to serve the `substanceContext` block · scientific opinions, screening-list memberships, use precedents and procedures under way attached to the substance. Served BY DEFAULT.

`context=false` drops it and saves four queries per substance · useful on a batch of fifty ingredients where only the applicable law is wanted, never to trim on principle.

⚠️ Only the literal value `false` drops the block; any other value (including `0` or `no`) leaves it served, and none is rejected.

On `/substances/lookup:batch`, use the `context: false` field of the BODY.

⚠️ Dropping the context says NOTHING about its content: a `substanceContext` that is null because you declined it does not mean "no opinion, no list". The same happens through `?sections=` when no toxicological or informative section is requested.

get.summary: The screening lists a substance belongs to
get.description:
Tells you which screening lists a substance belongs to (PFAS from the EPA inventory, IFRA standards), with a link to the reference document.

⚠️ **Membership imposes nothing on its own.** Being a PFAS or appearing in an IFRA standard does not make a substance forbidden: prohibitions and limits are _constraints_, retrieved via `/substances/lookup`.

⚠️ **No threshold or limit is returned here.** IFRA limits belong to a private association; this endpoint returns membership and the link to the document that carries them.

⚠️ **`substanceKnown: false`** means none of the given identifiers is in the index: the response then concludes nothing about membership in any list.

get.summary: A substance's impurity thresholds, per market
get.description:
A substance's impurity/contaminant thresholds (heavy metals, 1,4-dioxane, methanol…), market by market.

⚠️ **A "threshold" is not one number · SEVEN REGIMES coexist**, and confusing them yields a FALSE compliance verdict. The `regime` field states what exceeding means: `MANDATORY_LIMIT` (legal cap, finished product) · `GUIDANCE_LIMIT` (a recommendation, not law) · `COLORANT_PURITY_LIMIT` (on the RAW MATERIAL, never the finished product) · `LABELING_TRIGGER` (triggers a warning, not a ban) · `EXPOSURE_TRIGGER` (µg/day, never a ppm) · `PROHIBITION_TRACE_UNAVOIDABLE` (banned as an ingredient, trace tolerated if safe · NO number) · `NON_DETECTABLE` (a "not detected" requirement, NOT a ppm cap: no measurable quantity is tolerated, whatever your detection limit).

⚠️ **`matrix`** separates finished product from raw material; **`calculationBasis`** (e.g. `AS_ELEMENT`) decides the comparison.

⚠️ **No value is opposable until its `verificationLevel` is countersigned.**

get.description:

get.description:
Returns, for a market, the substances whose presence must be declared above a threshold (allergens), with the threshold text exactly as the legislator prints it. The `basisActs` field cites the reference acts: every row is traceable to its legal basis.

get.summary: What we have LEARNED since a given instant
get.description:
Returns what was added or updated in the corpus since a given instant. The time reference is KNOWLEDGE (`recordedFrom`), not the law: a text in force for two years but ingested yesterday appears here.

⚠️ **Page with `cursor`, never with `offset`, and never with your own clock.** Pass the previous response's `nextCursor` back after EVERY page, for as long as `truncated` is true. The feed is ordered oldest-first: an interrupted run resumes exactly where it stopped, and rows written mid-run are appended rather than shifting the pages under you.

Use this endpoint to keep an integration incrementally up to date.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Required. **ISO 8601 date-time in UTC**, `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ` (e.g. `2026-01-01T00:00:00Z`). It SETS the starting point of a sync; to continue one, pass `cursor` (the previous call's `nextCursor`), never your own clock nor `nextSince`. With `cursor`, `since` is still required but the cursor decides the place.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description:
Opaque **resume token**, the one the previous response returned in `nextCursor`. It is what pages this feed, not `offset`: pass it back verbatim, without parsing or rebuilding it. When supplied, it replaces `since` for filtering.

⚠️ **Why `since` alone is not enough**: several hundred constraints can share one timestamp down to the microsecond. A cursor that is only an instant cannot say where to resume INSIDE that batch · the loop then replays the same page forever. The token carries the instant AND the row.

parameters.name: legislator
parameters.description:
Legislator code (`EC`, `NMPA`, `MFDS`, `FDA`, `ANVISA`…). ⚠️ A referential DISTINCT from the territory one: the EU market is `EU`, its legislator is `EC`.

⚠️ An UNKNOWN code returns `400` (`unknown_legislator`, carrying the `knownLegislators` list). **Behaviour change on 2026-08-11**: the answer used to be a `200` with zero rows, which reads as "this legislator produced nothing" when in fact the code does not exist. This is the catalogue's costliest trap, because `/texts` is precisely the route one is pointed to in order to CONFIRM that a legislator code exists.

parameters.name: territory

ApiKeyHeader.description: The API key, prefixed `lab_`. ⚠️ Never in the URL: a query string ends up in the logs of every intermediary.

BearerApiKey.description: The same key, as `Authorization: Bearer lab_…`. Both forms are accepted.

error.description: Class code, stable and meant to be tested by the client.

message.description: Explanatory sentence. NEVER carries the server exception message: a Prisma error would expose table and column names.

knownTerritories.description: The territory codes actually known to the corpus. Served because a misspelled code would otherwise return zero results, which reads as "no constraint on this market", the opposite conclusion to the truth. ⚠️ This referential is the one of MARKETS, distinct from the one of LEGISLATORS (`knownLegislators`): the EU market is `EU`, its legislator is `EC` · mixing the two is the most frequent mistake.

knownLegislators.description: The legislator codes actually known to the corpus. ⚠️ A referential DISTINCT from the territory one: the EU market is `EU` but its legislator is `EC`; China is `CN` but its legislator is `NMPA`. A market code passed as `?legislator=` used to return zero rows and a `200`, that is "this legislator produced nothing", where there was only a mix-up between the two referentials.

grantedScopes.description: The scopes this key actually carries.

thinlyCoveredZones.description: The subscribed zones for which the corpus holds only a HANDFUL of constraints. Absent when there are none.

thinlyCoveredMeans.description: ⚠️ Never read silence on these markets as permission · the substance has not been checked against their full law, only against the little we hold.

impliedZones.description: Zones opened WITHOUT being in the contract, because a subscribed market is governed by their law (by reference or by membership). Absent when there are none.

impliedMeans.description: How to read `impliedZones` · present together with it.

unavailableZones.description: Zones of our nomenclature that are not offered today, because we do not yet hold extracted constraints for them. Distinct from `missingZones` (offered but not subscribed). Absent when there are none. ⚠️ An empty answer for these markets is NOT an absence of regulation.

unavailableMeans.description: How to read `unavailableZones` · present together with it.

closedMarkets.description: Markets (territory codes) included in the subscription but TEMPORARILY held back by RelayX. Absent when nothing is held back. ⚠️ Silence on these markets is NOT permission.

closedMeans.description: How to read `closedMarkets` · present together with it.

Abonnement.description: What the SUBSCRIPTION covers and does not, not to be confused with `withheldByScope`, which is a licence limit. A missing zone is a COMMERCIAL limit: this market's constraints exist and are not served. No COUNT is given for the missing zones, because computing it would require the very query the authorization forbids.

RetenuParPortee.description: Content that EXISTS and matches the query, but whose source text may not be redistributed under this key's scope. This is a LICENCE limit, NEVER an absence of regulation. `count > 0` reads "there is something here, request access", and certainly not "nothing to report".

territories.description: The markets concerned, NAMED. We say which ones, never what they contain.

RetenuParPorteeAvecTerritoires.description: Content that EXISTS and matches the query, but whose source text may not be redistributed under this key's scope. NotesLibres.description: The FREE-TEXT notes of this API are written in French, the language of the operators who record them, and are NOT machine-translated: they carry regulatory findings, and a translation no one wrote would be worth less than a note we know still needs translating. Every ENUMERATED field and every `*Means` explanation is in English.

officialRef.description: The act's reference. Always served: citing an act number is a public legal fact, and hiding it would break amendment traceability.

title.description: The title belongs to the work: it is served only if the act's redistribution right allows it. `null` together with `titleWithheld` means WITHHELD, never "this act has no title".

titleWithheld.description: Present only when the title is withheld.

ruleType.description: `MAX_CONCENTRATION`, `PROHIBITION`, `LABEL_WARNING`, `AGE_RESTRICTION`, `PROFESSIONAL_ONLY`, `MIXTURE_LIMIT`, `PH_CONDITION`, `PURITY_LIMIT` · plus ⚠️ `MAX_DAILY_DOSE`: a daily DOSE in µg/day (California Prop 65), bounding EXPOSURE and NOT the content of a formula. Comparing it to a formula percentage compares two different quantities. Filter on this type to keep it out of any content calculation: that is exactly why it is a distinct type.

derivationStatus.description: `DERIVED`: a single limit was read without ambiguity. `AMBIGUOUS`: we looked and REFUSED to choose. ⚠️ A missing number is the information, not a gap: never read that absence as "no limit".

calculationBasis.description: ⚠️ Decides as much as the value: "5 % expressed as acid" is NOT "5 % of the substance". An integration that compares a dosage without reading this field is silently wrong.

minValue.description: ⚠️ A LOWER bound when `boundKind` says so · never a ceiling. Read `boundKind` BEFORE using this value: confusing the two inverts the rule.

boundKind.description: What the value bounds · `MIN`, `MAX`, or `null` where the text does not say. ⚠️ A `null` alongside a `minValue` is a known GAP, not licence to guess: read `sourceFragment`.

effectiveFrom.description: Date from which the rule takes effect, where it differs from the entry's.

productCategories.description: Product categories targeted · empty when the rule does not discriminate.

warningText.description: The wording to PRINT, carried by `LABEL_WARNING` rules.

sourceFragment.description: The EXACT fragment of text the rule is drawn from: enough to verify without taking our word.

derivationStatus.description: `DERIVED` only if the WHOLE branch was recognized.

appliesToAllCosmetics.description: ⚠️ `true` only if the text SAYS so. An unread text yields `false`: "not stated", never "everywhere". Confusing the two would apply a narrow restriction to a whole range.

excludes.description: The text's reservations. Served only when the WHOLE reservation was read: a clean inclusion paired with a silent exclusion would apply the limit to the very products the legislator carves out.

PorteeProduitStructuree.description: The STRUCTURED product scope. ⚠️ Named `productScopeStructured` and not `productScope`: the latter exists under `literal.productScope` and carries the raw text. ⚠️ A scope we could not read is NOT a universal scope: the raw text remains the reference in every case.

minValue.description: ⚠️ The LOWER bound. `minValue` WITHOUT `maxValue` is a FLOOR · the text requires AT LEAST this level and sets no upper limit. Reading it as a ceiling INVERTS the requirement: an under-dosed formulation would look compliant and nothing would ever flag it (a wrong ceiling eventually surfaces, an inverted floor does not). Read `boundKind`.

boundKind.description: `MAXIMUM` (ceiling), `MINIMUM` (floor ONLY), `RANGE` (permitted band: BOTH bounds are law · below the lower one the active is not effective, above the upper one it is no longer recognised as safe). `null` when the rule is not `DERIVED`.

phMin.description: The limit only holds within this pH window · "11 % (as thioglycolic acid) with a pH ≤ 9.5" is not the same limit outside it.

effectiveFrom.description: ⚠️ The value only takes effect on this date (YYYY-MM-DD). Serving it as a current ceiling would answer a question about a DIFFERENT day. Not to be confused with the ENTRY dates, which live in `applicability`.

LimiteDeBranche.description: The NUMERIC limit of THIS branch. ⚠️ It neither replaces nor contradicts `rules[]`: `rules[]` answers "does this CONSTRAINT carry a single limit?", this one "does this BRANCH carry one?". Confusing them would suggest a contradiction where there are two granularities.

concentrationIsShared.description: True when ONE limit governs all branches.

minValue.description: ⚠️ The LOWER bound. `minValue` WITHOUT `maxValue` is a FLOOR · the text requires AT LEAST this level and sets no upper limit. Reading it as a ceiling INVERTS the requirement: an under-dosed formulation would look compliant and nothing would ever flag it (a wrong ceiling eventually surfaces, an inverted floor does not). Read `boundKind`.

boundKind.description: `MAXIMUM` (ceiling), `MINIMUM` (floor ONLY), `RANGE` (permitted band: BOTH bounds are law · below the lower one the active is not effective, above the upper one it is no longer recognised as safe). `null` when the rule is not `DERIVED`.

sourceFragment.description: The EXACT text fragment the rule comes from · enough to check it without taking our word.

appliesToAllCosmetics.description: ⚠️ True ONLY if the text SAYS "all cosmetics". An unread text yields `false` · "not stated", never "everywhere".

excludes.description: What the text REMOVES from scope. Served only when the reservation was read IN FULL: a clean inclusion paired with a silent exclusion would apply the limit to products the legislator carves out.

segmentationMethod.description: HOW the split was obtained · `LABELLED_BOTH_COLUMNS` (strongest), `LABELLED_LIMIT_ONLY`, `LABELLED_SCOPE_ONLY`, `INLINE_DISCRIMINANT`, `STRUCTURED_KEY_VALUE`, `SINGLE`, and ⚠️ `POSITIONAL_SEPARATOR` which pairs BY POSITION rather than by label · structurally weaker, check it against `literal`.

rulesCombinator.description: Always `ALL_OF` · the rules of a case are CUMULATIVE.

combinator.description: Always `EXCLUSIVE_OR` · exactly ONE case applies to a given product.

Cas_Bloc.description: ⚠️ **Cases are ALTERNATIVE, the rules within a case are CUMULATIVE.** That is the one sentence to remember. EU Annex III writes "(a) 3.0 % (b) 2.0 % (c) 0.5 %": three regimes by product type, exactly ONE of which governs your formula. Annex V instead sets a 0.5 % limit together with three prohibitions that ALL hold at once. ⚠️ This block does not replace `rules[]` nor contradict it: `rules[]` says whether the ENTRY has a single limit, `cases[]` says which regime applies to YOUR product. `null` when the entry has neither scope nor limit to segment · a blanket ban, for instance.

PorteeProduitBranches.description: The MATCHED branches: a scope, its limit. ⚠️ Matching is by LABEL, never by rank: matching by rank would attach a real limit to the wrong product. `null` when the constraint carries a single branch: there is then nothing to match, which is not a refusal.

consolidatedVersion.description: ⚠️ CELEX of the CONSOLIDATED version this row is extracted from. `officialRef` and `publicationDate` describe the ORIGINAL act (accurate, and misleading on its own: a 2009 act whose annexes have been amended dozens of times since). `null` means no consolidation was recorded for this row: read `text.sourceUrl` and `provenance` rather than assuming the act's date.

sourceUrlKind.description: What this address lets you verify: `OFFICIAL_TEXT` leads to the text; an authority portal grounds no claim of completeness.

basisProvision.description: The NATIONAL provision that makes the reference.

referencedScope.description: What the reference bears on, as the act designates it.

referenceNature.description: `DYNAMIC` (the law follows amendments) or `STATIC` (frozen at one version).

alsoAppliesIn.description: ⚠️ The territories where THIS entry also applies, by REFERENCE from a national act · the law there is borrowed, not enacted.

printedByText.description: True if a LEGISLATOR wrote this value · false if we completed it from an inventory.

linkedSubstances.description: Every name and number we hold for the substances this entry covers · these are what you match a catalogue against. ⚠️ This is NOT what the act prints: that is `identifiers`, and it is the only form to cite. Capped at 25 substances per entry and 40 values per substance.

linkedSubstancesTruncated.description: ⚠️ True if this entry covers MORE substances than the list carries. Only FAMILY entries are ever concerned · the longest in the corpus links 301 substances ("Cells, tissues or products of human origin"), the next 129 (trialkylamines). Served even when false: its absence would read as "complete list", which is exactly what makes a reader conclude "this ingredient is not covered" about an entry that covers it.

logicalEntryId.description: The STABLE identifier of the entry across its versions, the key for `/entries/{logicalEntryId}/history`. ⚠️ `entryRef` cannot play this role: "III/224" designates a PLACE in an annex, which two successive versions share.

annexRef.description: The reference as the LEGISLATOR writes it. China prints "表4 化妆品准用防腐剂", Korea "Annex 2 Table 1": serving "Annex V" instead would name an annex that exists nowhere in their law. ⚠️ NEVER use this to compare two markets · `annexType` carries the normalised meaning.

annexRefEn.description: The same reference in ENGLISH · "Table 4 · Permitted preservatives" for the Chinese example. Same pattern as `literalName` / `literalNameEn` for substances: a literal is not translated, it is DOUBLED. ⚠️ Mirrors `annexRef` when the reference is already English; `null` when no English form has been ESTABLISHED from the source · never a guessed translation.

annexTypeMeans.description: ⚠️ The legend travels WITH the value. `INVENTORY_LISTED` reads spontaneously as "listed, therefore authorized" whereas an inventory says nothing about authorization: it is the ABSENCE, not the presence, that carries a consequence there.

entryScope.description: Does the entry target ONE substance or a GROUP? A group ("X and its salts") covers derivatives the client did not search for.

matchedBy.description: The parameters that brought THIS row up · `cas`, `ec`, `inci`, `name`.

reachedViaGroupEntry.description: ⚠️ True if the row was reached through the INDEX rather than because the act prints your number · typically a GROUP entry. Read its `literal` before citing it.

entryRefKind.description: `OFFICIAL`, `CONSTRUCTED` or `MISSING`. ⚠️ Served on EVERY constraint, including official ones: a field that appears only on problematic cases would let you conclude from its absence.

annexRefKind.description: `PRINTED_BY_SOURCE`, `OUR_LABEL` or `UNVERIFIED` · the SYMMETRIC half of `entryRefKind`, for the SCOPE reference. ⚠️ All 1,239 US constraints carry `Annex II`, `Annex III` or `Annex IV`: no US cosmetics regime (neither 21 CFR nor any State statute) is organised in annexes. The citation the source does print is in `entryRefNote`.

nature.description: `DERIVED_BY_LAW` must be visible: an inferred prohibition does not have the same evidential status as a literal annex entry.

derivedFrom.description: ⚠️ The entry this one is DERIVED FROM · its PREMISE. Present only when the derivation exists. The typical case: an `art.15-...` entry banned in cosmetics is derived from the matching CLP classification entry (`Annex VI Table 3`). ⚠️⚠️ It tells you WHERE TO READ THE PREMISE, never the verdict: the cited entry carries its OWN conditions and a DIFFERENT legal status · a CMR classification bans nothing in cosmetics by itself, it is Article 15 of Regulation 1223/2009 that DRAWS the ban from it. Cite it alongside `derivationLegalBasis`. ⚠️ NOT to be confused with `supersededByVersionId` (the NEXT VERSION of the SAME entry) nor with `coveredBy` (a BROADER entry that absorbed this one). When the citation cannot be served (the entry sits outside the market this response covers), the fields are null and `means` says so: this is NOT "derived from nothing", it is a withheld citation.

casList.description: The `cas` literal SPLIT when it carries several numbers · `null` when it carries one. Only WELL-FORMED values are kept: a fragment that is not a number has no place in a list of numbers. The literal stays intact in `cas`.

ecList.description: The `ec` literal SPLIT when it carries several numbers · `null` otherwise.

inciList.description: The `inci` literal SPLIT when it carries several names · `null` otherwise. ⚠️ It has its own splitting rule: **a comma is never a CAS or EC separator, and it IS an INCI one** ("Ammonium benzoate, calcium benzoate, …"), while the same field uses a slash in the EU and a semicolon in the UK. A comma preceded by a digit stays a nomenclature locant and does not split. ⚠️ No shape filter, unlike `casList`: an INCI name is validated by no check digit, and requiring a shape would silence botanical extracts and mixtures.

fullText.description: The entry's full text, as cited. ⚠️ NULL when the source publishes the entry as a STRUCTURED RECORD rather than prose: that record's fields are then in `sourceRecordFields`, never here. This field carries only the legislator's wording.

sourceRecordFields.description: The SOURCE RECORD's own fields, where the source publishes a structured record (US State lists, Prop 65, OTC monographs): `toxicity_type`, `listing_mechanism`, `date_listed`, `ban_type`… ⚠️ Served BESIDE the literal, not inside it: these are record attributes, not the legislator's wording. For the citable text of these rows, read `entryRefNote`.

language.description: The language of `original`. ⚠️ Without it, the pair `{original, en}` reads as "the original is not English", false for most texts, whose `en` is null BECAUSE the original IS English. ⚠️ It describes the SOURCE ACT: when `provenance` is `EDITORIAL`, the sentences served are ours and may be in a language other than the one announced here.

provenance.description: ⚠️ `QUOTED` or `EDITORIAL`. `EDITORIAL` means this block carries OUR prose, not the legislator's, and it covers TWO cases. First case: the entry has **no printed text** · it is DERIVED by operation of law (a substance classified CMR under CLP is banned in cosmetics by Article 15 of Regulation 1223/2009, with no annex listing it), and every sentence served is ours. Second case: a LITERAL entry can be `EDITORIAL` too · 8,979 rows (Chinese inventory, Canadian CCCR) do quote their source in `concentration`, `productScope` and `warnings`, but carry OUR note in `conditions` · kept because no quotation replaces it, and because without it a listing on a POSITIVE list would read as an authorisation. ⚠️ The language of our sentences may differ from `language`, which describes the SOURCE ACT and not this text. Never cite them as law: cite `history.originatedBy`. `means` states which of the three cases applies.

means.description: The sentence stating which of the three cases applies · `QUOTED`, `EDITORIAL` (a derived entry) or `MIXED` (a literal entry where only `conditions` is ours), and what may then be quoted. Served in English. ⚠️ ABSENT in `view=standard` and `view=summary`, which strip every `means` key.

ref.description: The marker as printed in the table · "17", "18".

anyOf.description: The NORMAL shape, served by the EU and the United Kingdom.

texte.description: The note's text, quoted in hangul.

renvoieA.description: The annex the note redirects to · "별표 2".

anyOf.description: ⚠️ A DEVIANT shape, with French keys and NOT wrapped in an array · served today by Korea alone. It will be normalised to the shape above; handle it in the meantime, do not expect it forever.

regulatoryFootnotes.description:
The table footnotes of the official text. A note that redirects to ANOTHER annex and is not served turns a partial rule into a complete one · Annex V entries 17 and 18 carry a MUTUAL EXCLUSION rule between two preservatives, without which one believes they can be combined.

⚠️ **TWO shapes** are served today: an array of `{ref, text}` objects (EU, GB) and a bare `{renvoi, texte, renvoieA}` object (Korea). Test the shape before reading · indexing straight into the array fails on the Korean row.

⚠️ `null` means "no note attached to this row", never "the table carries none".

startDateMeans.description: Why the start date is `null` · it is UNKNOWN, not legally absent. ⚠️ Never read this emptiness as "in force since forever".

precision.description: `UNKNOWN` means the start date is a sentinel: the constraint is served on the cautious side, but no NEGATIVE verdict should rely on it.

verificationNote.description: A doubt about the LAW. Written in French.

errataNote.description: A KNOWN defect in OUR OWN handling of this row, written in French. Not to be confused with `verificationNote`, which carries a doubt about the LAW; this one carries a doubt about US. An example served today: "NIFDC's official API prints CERAMIDE NG at 序号 6014; we serve CERAMIDE EOP" · a dossier citing our number would cite the wrong one. ⚠️ The literal value is NOT silently corrected: the discrepancy is declared and you decide. Only errata that concern you are served; internal maintenance notes are withheld.

chemicalName.description: The chemical name, as the text prints it.

colourIndex.description: The Colour Index number (`CI 77491`…), where the entry carries one.

inciIecic.description: ⚠️ The CHINESE inventory (IECIC) name · this is NOT the EU INCI, and the two diverge. Read `inciEu` for the Union.

inciEu.description: The INCI name carried by CosIng, the European Commission inventory, for the linked substance.

inciUs.description: The US label name, served ONLY where a US source states one. Today that is the FDA colour additive listing, which prints the label name ("FD&C Green No. 3") next to its Colour Index number. ⚠️ `null` does NOT mean the ingredient is unlisted or unlawful in the US: INCI is a single international nomenclature, and outside these cases the EU name applies.

labelMixed.description: The dual-market LABEL form, slash-separated. ⚠️ This is NOT an INCI name, which is why the field is not called `inci…`: for a COLORANT the EU side is the Colour Index number ("CI 16035/FD&C Red No. 40"). Annex IV of Reg. 1223/2009 lists colorants BY CI number and Article 19 admits that form in the ingredient list · a CI number is lawful on an EU pack and is still not an INCI. ⚠️ Served only where the two markets genuinely name the ingredient differently. Where it is `null`, no dual form is attested · do not build one by concatenating the other fields.

labelMixedParenthetical.description: The SAME pair of names as `labelMixed`, written with brackets: "AQUA (WATER)". Brands use one form or the other depending on house style, and serving only one would force half of integrators to rebuild the other. Both fields are derived from the same `inciEu` and `inciUs` · nothing is stored twice. ⚠️ This field is `null` when either name ALREADY contains brackets (the US dictionary puts the common name in them), because the nested form "A (B (C) D)" is neither readable nor re-parsable · use `labelMixed`, which is always available in that case.

synonyms.description: ALTERNATIVE names published by CosIng ("Deionized Water", "Purified Water", "Sea Salt"). ⚠️ They do not say what the substance IS · they say what it gets called elsewhere. Use them to recognise an ingredient in a supplier document that uses neither the INCI nor the chemical name. Never put one on a pack. EMPTY array when none is published.

nomenclature.description: The INCI names OUR index attaches to the linked substance, by MARKET. ⚠️ This block is ENRICHED, not extracted: `identifiers` carries what the act itself prints. It is also excluded from `changedFields` on `/entries/{logicalEntryId}/history`, because a link we made is not an amendment by the legislator.

Contrainte.description: ⚠️ This shape · and the `required` list above · describes the `full` view, the DEFAULT of `/substances/lookup`. In `view=standard` the same shape is served without the prose (every `means` key or key ending in `Means`, even though declared required here) and without `literal.fullText`. In `view=summary` this is no longer the shape at all: see `ContrainteResumee`.

inci.description: ⚠️ A fallback applied in THIS view only: when the act prints no INCI, the ENRICHED value from `nomenclature.inciEu` is served here, with nothing marking it as such. In `full` and `standard`, `identifiers.inci` stays what the text prints and the enrichment lives in `nomenclature`.

concentration.description: The concentration text AS PRINTED (`literal.concentration.original`). It is the authority · `maxValue` is only a reading of it.

maxValue.description: ⚠️ Served ONLY from a `DERIVED` rule. `null` does NOT mean "no limit": it means no single rule could be read unambiguously · read `concentration` instead. When several `DERIVED` rules coexist, this view shows only ONE (the first): switch to `view=standard` or `full` to get them all.

calculationBasis.description: ⚠️ Decides as much as the value: "5 % expressed as acid" is NOT "5 % of the substance".

regulator.description: The authority that issues the text. ⚠️ It is an OBJECT, not a string · read `regulator.code`.

ContrainteResumee.description: The FLAT shape served by `?view=summary`. ⚠️ It is not a truncated `Contrainte`: the `literal`, `rules`, `cases`, `productScopeStructured`, `history`, `validity` and `provenance` blocks are ABSENT, not empty. Conclude nothing from that · ask for `view=standard` or `view=full` to get them.

en.description: ⚠️ The OFFICIAL English version, never a translation of our own making. `null` means "the legislator publishes none", not "we have not translated it".

knownFrom.description: Since when WE know this (ISO 8601 date-time, UTC). The time of KNOWLEDGE, not that of the law.

knownUntil.description: ⚠️ `null` means "this is what we know TODAY", NEVER "date unknown". A client who confused the two would misdate a repeal.

isCurrent.description: ⚠️ Is `false` as soon as a version is RETRACTED, even when `knownUntil` is `null`. A retraction says "this version was WRONG", not "we stopped knowing it": the two are not the same. See `retracted`.

retracted.description: Set when WE withdrew this version because it was wrong · a mistake on our side, not a repeal by the legislator. `null` otherwise.

supersededByVersionId.description: The version that superseded this one, when it exists.

supersessionNature.description: What the act changed · `RULE_CHANGED` the LAW (the new version applies from that act) · `WORDING_RESTATED` only the WORDING (the rule already applied; do not date the obligation from that act) · `UNDETERMINED` nobody has established which. ⚠️ `UNDETERMINED` does NOT mean "nothing changed".

supersessionMeans.description: The same distinction spelled out, served next to the value · a category without its meaning forces the consumer to interpret it, and on an obligation date that is where wrong conclusions come from. Null when the entry has no next version.

coveredBy.description: ⚠️ The BROADER entry that absorbed this one · NOT to be confused with `supersededByVersionId`. That one is the NEXT VERSION of THE SAME entry, which keeps existing; this one is a DIFFERENT entry, the one to read from now on because this entry ceased to exist under its own number. ⚠️⚠️ It tells you WHERE TO LOOK, never the verdict: the covering entry carries its OWN conditions and may just as well PROHIBIT as permit. Only its CITATION is served, never its content · copying that across would suggest its conditions apply here.

values.description: The fields THIS list publishes · their shape depends on the list, read `list` before interpreting them.

valuesWithheld.description: ⚠️ `true` when the list is under a restrictive licence: membership is served, its PAYLOAD is not. Missing `values` with this flag is not missing data, it is a redistribution right we do not hold.

listedName.description: The name carried by the LIST, often different from the corpus one.

entryUrl.description: The substance's record in the list, or failing that the list itself.

means.description: ⚠️ What membership means, and above all what it does NOT impose.

cas.description: The CAS identifier received, or `null` if it was not provided.

substanceKnown.description: ⚠️ `false`: none of the identifiers is in the corpus index, and the response then says NOTHING.

ReponseCriblage.description: A substance's screening lists. ⚠️ Membership, never obligation.

regime.description: ⚠️ The regime decides what exceeding MEANS. A legal cap, a guidance, a colorant purity, a labelling trigger, an exposure dose and a prohibition-without-a-number are NOT compared the same way.

maxValue.description: `null` for regimes without a number (prohibition-no-number, non-detectable).

maxUnit.description: `PPM`/`MG_KG`/`PERCENT`, or `UG_DAY` (µg/day, Prop 65 exposure · NOT a concentration).

calculationBasis.description: E.g. `AS_ELEMENT` ("expressed as Pb element") · decides the comparison against the measured value.

matrix.description: ⚠️ Finished product vs raw material. Comparing a colorant limit to a finished product yields a FALSE verdict.

applicableFrom.description: Date from which this limit applies. `null` = already applicable, or no such date.

applicableUntil.description: Date on which it ceases to apply. `null` = no known end.

inForceToday.description: ⚠️ COMPUTED on each response, never frozen in the database · a date passes on its own, a frozen boolean does not. `false` means "not yet" or "no longer", and `timingMeans` says which.

timingMeans.description: WHAT the date means for a verdict about today · a limit not yet in force is served so you can prepare, never so you can apply it.

verificationLevel.description: ⚠️ `UNVERIFIED`: the value is not opposable until it has been countersigned against the primary text.

ReponseSeuilsImpurete.description: A substance's impurity thresholds, per market and PER REGIME.

body.description: The body that publishes. It decides the redistribution regime of the DOCUMENT at the end of the link; the present row, itself, is a citation, which is free.

reference.description: The reference as the body publishes it. ⚠️ The source set sometimes puts a whole title there: it is served as-is and is not presumed to be a code.

status.description: Added 2026-10-21. The state of the version in force: `FINAL`, `PRELIMINARY` (open for comments), `REQUEST` (mandate: the Commission has seized the committee, nothing is concluded · served in `pendingRequests`, never in `opinions`). `null` = not qualified (bodies other than the SCCS).

adoptedOn.description: Added 2026-10-21. Date the committee ADOPTED the version in force (YYYY-MM-DD).

publishedOn.description: PUBLICATION date by the body (YYYY-MM-DD). ⚠️ For SCCS opinions it used to carry the adoption date, now in `adoptedOn`. Opinions re-read on their official page (finals since 2025, then as re-reads proceed) carry the publication here; for older ones it still equals `adoptedOn`.

versions.description: Added 2026-10-21. The opinion's history: preliminary, final, corrigenda. An SCCS opinion keeps the same reference from preliminary to final · the row carries the version in force, this array everything that preceded or corrected it.

sourceUrl.description: The document's address. It is what gives the row its value: without it, the opinion would be an unverifiable assertion.

redistributionRight.description: What the body's LICENCE allows you to do with the document at the end of the link.

cas.description: The CAS identifier received, or `null` if it was not provided.

pendingRequests.description: Added 2026-10-21. Pending MANDATES (“Request for a scientific Opinion”): an assessment has been requested, no opinion has been delivered yet. Excluded from `opinions` and `total`.

means.description: What the list says, and what it does not.

ReponseAvisScientifiques.description: The scientific opinions attached to a substance (resolved from CAS, EC or INCI). ⚠️ No text, no limit, no verdict: the fact and the link.

name.description: The name as printed by the legislator.

nameEn.description: The OFFICIAL English version when it exists.

entryRef.description: The annex entry reference, citable against the official text.

declarationThreshold.description: ⚠️ The threshold as PRINTED, in text. A single sentence usually carries BOTH thresholds (rinse-off and leave-on): deriving a number from it is a derivation that was not done, and a figure fabricated here would be compared against a real concentration.

basisActs.description: ⚠️ The acts the list is DRAWN from. This is what makes it reproducible and citable: every row traces back to the regulation that inscribed it.

basisRule.description: `INTRODUCED_BY_ACT` · the entries an act inscribed. `DUTY_STATED_IN_THE_ENTRY` · those whose own text carries the declaration duty.

basisAnnexes.description: ⚠️ The annexes retained · the OTHER half of the criterion. An amending act usually touches several annexes, and only the restricted-substances one carries a declaration duty.

scanCapped.description: ⚠️ True if the scan reached its cap · the list is then SHORT without saying so.

means.description: What the list says, and what it does not.

ReponseAllergenes.description: A market's individually-declarable substances, derived from the corpus's amendment attribution. ⚠️ An empty list on a market outside your subscription is not an absence of obligation: read `subscription`.

role.description: `UNION` · the territory is the union itself. `MEMBER` · it is a member of one.

transpositionMode.description: ⚠️ `DIRECT` · the corpus applies as it stands. `REQUIRES_NATIONAL_ACT` · it binds NO ONE until a national act has incorporated it, and incorporation is not uniform across members.

territory.description: The territory that REFERS to this corpus.

basisProvision.description: The NATIONAL provision carrying the reference · citable as it stands.

referencedScope.description: ⚠️ WHAT the reference reaches, and nothing more. A reference bounded to Annexes II–VI does not make the rest of the corpus applicable.

referenceNature.description: The nature of the reference · static to a dated version, or dynamic to the law in force.

means.description: What the nature of the reference commits to, in plain words.

referencedTerritory.description: The territory whose law this market APPLIES.

referencedScope.description: ⚠️ What the reference reaches, and nothing more.

referencedBy.description: The territories whose NATIONAL act refers to this corpus · the law applies there by BORROWING.

appliesByReference.description: The corpora THIS market applies by reference. Absent when there are none.

borrowedConstraintCount.description: The entries that bind this market WITHOUT being printed by it (by reference). Not added to `constraintCount`. Absent at zero.

status.description: ⚠️ Two kinds. `PROHIBITED` and `RESTRICTED` are POSITIVE findings, citable against the official text. `AUTHORIZED` is a statement of ABSENCE, served only on a market whose ALL coverage scopes are countersigned complete. `INSUFFICIENT_DATA` means "nothing found, and this absence proves nothing", never "probably authorized".

statusBasis.description: On WHAT the status rests. `POSITIVE_FINDING`: an entry exists. `COUNTERSIGNED_COVERAGE`: the absence is opposable because a named human has countersigned the completeness of the coverage scope. `INCOMPLETE_COVERAGE`: the absence is not established. `CMR_CLASSIFICATION_PRESENT`: no prohibition was found, but a harmonised CMR 1A/1B classification is served · Article 15 prohibits such substances save for a derogation, and the status is `INSUFFICIENT_DATA`. `WITHHELD_BY_IDENTIFIER`: constraints linked to the substance were withheld because their text prints a DIFFERENT number in the field you searched · the status is `INSUFFICIENT_DATA`, and `statusMeans` names the numbers to query.

statusMeans.description: The sentence that says what this status lets you conclude. It is served on EVERY row, including the normal case: a field that appears only on awkward cases would let you conclude from its absence. ⚠️ It also carries, where there are any, the disclosure of the entries set aside from the verdict (see `nonCosmeticEntryCount`): that disclosure sits next to the status rather than elsewhere, because this is where the misreading happens.

constraintCount.description: Number of constraints found on this market. ⚠️ It counts EVERY entry found, including those that do not govern a cosmetic and are therefore excluded from `status` (see `nonCosmeticEntryCount`). `constraintCount > 0` alongside an `INSUFFICIENT_DATA` status is therefore not a contradiction.

nonCosmeticEntryCount.description: The number of entries of this market that NAME the substance but govern a non-cosmetic product (paints, air fresheners, insecticides…). ⚠️ They are EXCLUDED from `status` · a rule about paint does not bind a cream · and they are NOT removed for all that: they stay counted in `constraintCount`, listed in `annexTypes` and `entryRefs`, and served in full by `/substances/lookup?territory=…`, where each carries its own `productStatus`. ⚠️ The field is ABSENT when the count is zero: its absence means "no entry set aside", never "not checked".

nonCosmeticMeans.description: The sentence that says what to do with that count, served with it and absent with it. It names the route that returns those entries and the field to read on them (`productStatus`), so that a gap between `constraintCount` and the status gets verified rather than guessed.

annexTypes.description: The kinds of listing encountered. ⚠️ `CLP_HARMONISED` is a HAZARD classification, not a cosmetic rule, and `INVENTORY_LISTED` says an ingredient has already been used: neither restricts use, which is why they do not produce a `RESTRICTED` status.

entryRefs.description: The entry references that ground the status, capped at 20.

entryRefsTruncated.description: True if some references were cut.

scopesTotal.description: Number of regulatory coverage scopes described for this market.

allComplete.description: True only if EVERY scope is countersigned complete. This is the condition for an `AUTHORIZED` status.

byCompleteness.description: Count of scopes by completeness level (`COMPLETE`, `PARTIAL`, `NOT_EXTRACTED`).

incompleteScopes.description: ⚠️ The scopes whose completeness is NOT established, named (e.g. "Annex VI Table 3"). An absence of result on any of them proves nothing. Capped at 50.

incompleteScopesTruncated.description: True if the incomplete-scopes list was cut at 50.

coverage.description: Summary of this market's coverage. Tells you whether an absence of result is conclusive.

asOf.description: The LAW date at which the response was computed.

searchMeans.description: What the search actually covered · and, when ALL rows were reached by NAME alone, the warning that says so and names the CAS numbers to query for an anchored answer.

upcoming.description: The constraints NOT in force at `asOf` that will be · same shape as the `upcoming` of `/substances/lookup`. Absent when there are none.

identifierCaveats.description: What the search key could REACH, and what it left out.

identifierResolution.description: WHAT EACH PARAMETER became · submitted, normalised, recognised or not, malformed or not. ⚠️ An empty `markets` alongside `malformed: true` is a faulty INPUT, never a statement about the law.

truncated.description: ⚠️ True when the substance carries more than 600 constraints: this summary may then MISS an entire market.

ReponseResumeMarches.description: A PER-MARKET summary, with no regulatory text. The detail is pulled market by market with `/substances/lookup?territory=…`.

truncated.description: True if the block holds more items than those returned.

means.description: ⚠️ What this block commits to, and above all what it does NOT. Read it before reporting any of its items as a constraint.

ContexteSubstance.description:
The signals ATTACHED to the substance, none of them binding law · scientific opinions (CIR, SCCS, WHO), screening-list memberships, concentrations ALREADY ASSESSED on a market, and regulatory procedures UNDER WAY.

⚠️ An opinion is not a rule. A screening-list membership forbids nothing. A use precedent authorises nothing. An open procedure binds nothing today. Each block carries its own `means` · that is where the nuance lives.

`context=false` sets this block to `null` · a `substanceContext` that is null because you did not ask for it says NOTHING about its content. `?sections=` removes the blocks you did not request.

submitted.description: The value AS YOU SENT IT.

normalized.description: The form the search actually ran on.

malformed.description: ⚠️ True if the value CANNOT be an identifier of that type · wrong check digit, impossible shape. A malformed search returning zero says nothing about the law.

resolved.description: True if the identifier was recognised by the index.

territoryScope.description: Present when `territory` is given. `APPLICABLE` (default): `included` names the unions of direct application and the territories borrowed by regime reference whose rows are served. `TERRITORY_ONLY` (`territoryOnly=true`): `excluded` names what ALSO applies in the territory and is NOT served.

asOf.description: The LAW date at which the response was computed (YYYY-MM-DD).

asOfMeans.description: ⚠️ Served when `asOf` carries a PAST date · never read an empty result at an early date as "unregulated then".

identifierResolution.description: WHAT EACH PARAMETER became · submitted, normalised, recognised or not, malformed or not.

searchMeans.description: ⚠️ WHAT the search key used reaches, and what it does not. A search by identifier does not touch GROUP entries, which often carry no number yet cover the requested substance.

identifierAgreement.description: Present when SEVERAL identifiers are submitted: `AGREEING` if they designate the same substance, `CONFLICTING` otherwise (the constraints of both are then served, merged).

printedNumbers.description: The numbers those entries print (at most 20) · query them separately.

withheldByIdentifier.description: The entries linked to the substance and WITHHELD because their text prints a DIFFERENT number in the field searched. Absent when nothing is withheld.

truncated.description: True if rows remain beyond this page.

scanCapped.description: True if the pre-scan reached its cap: `total` is then a LOWER BOUND.

appliesFrom.description: Date it takes effect (YYYY-MM-DD), in flat form · `validity` carries the whole window.

appliesFromPrecision.description: Says whether the date was READ in the act or DERIVED.

constraints.description: Constraints NOT in force at `asOf` but that will be · deliberately outside `constraints`, because a verdict for today must not count them. Each row is a COMPLETE constraint: `logicalEntryId`, `cases`, `rules`, `literal`, `text`, `validity`, `regulatoryFootnotes`. ⚠️ Two blocks are dropped, for one reason: `linkedSubstances` and `nomenclature` are ENRICHMENT already served on the in-force constraints of the same response, and repeating them would double the payload. `matchedBy` and `reachedViaGroupEntry` describe how a SEARCH found a row · this block is not one.

identifierCaveats.description: Present only when a parameter was widened, ignored or resolved through a partial index. Its absence means no caveat weighs on the identifiers used.

means.description: What these entries are, and what they are not.

name.description: Name as printed by the entry.

cas.description: CAS as printed by the entry.

otherNameMatches.description: Present only when entries CONTAIN your term inside a longer name (derivative, ester, salt named on its own, copolymer, blend) and our index does not link them to the substance you asked for. They are in NEITHER `constraints` NOR `total`.

status.description: `HAS_DATA`: entries exist (served, upcoming, or withheld by your scope). `KNOWN_WITHOUT_DATA`: we know the ingredient (substance index or ingredient catalogue) and no entry was found on the markets queried · this is NEVER an authorisation. `UNKNOWN_IDENTIFIER`: we do not know this identifier · nothing can be concluded. `NOT_SEARCHED`: all or part of the input was not searched (see `identifierResolution`) · this zero says nothing.

means.description: The sentence to read, in the negotiated language.

name.description: The name as the source publishes it.

casNumbers.description: The CAS numbers the source prints (empty if none).

source.description: The public source naming the ingredient.

sourceRef.description: The originating row in the source ("CosIng 88287").

readAt.description: Date the row was read at the source.

knownFrom.description: Present when the ingredient is known ONLY from our identity catalogue (no substance record) · identity only, no regulatory data.

positiveListMarkets.description: The markets of your contract (or the requested territory) that keep a POSITIVE list: an absence there is TO BE VERIFIED (not authorised, or subject to a prior filing), never "unrestricted". Read `/coverage` (`absenceMeans`) scope by scope.

ingredientStatus.description: What the answer means for this ingredient: data, known ingredient without data, or unknown identifier. An empty answer no longer has to be guessed.

baseName.description: The derived base form (stereochemical descriptor, salt or hydrate removed).

descriptors.description: What distinguishes the submitted form from its base.

constraintCount.description: Number of base-form constraints visible with THIS key.

query.description: The query to run to see them.

means.description: The sentence to read, in the negotiated language.

baseForm.description: Present ONLY for a name search (`inci` or `name`, without `cas` or `ec`) whose name carries a stereochemical descriptor (L-, D-, DL-, cis-, trans-, (R)-…), a salt (HCl) or a hydrate, AND whose base form has constraints. It is a POINTER: those constraints are not served, and whether they apply to the submitted form is not established.

sectionsReturned.description: Present ONLY when `?sections=` narrowed the response: the list of blocks actually served. A block missing from this list was OMITTED, not emptied.

sectionsMeans.description: Present with `sectionsReturned`: a reminder that an unrequested block is ABSENT, not empty. Its absence means nothing.

constraints.description: The shape of the items depends on `?view=`: `Contrainte` in `full` (the default) and in `standard` (without the prose and without `literal.fullText`), `ContrainteResumee` in `summary`. This response's `view` field states which one you hold · its absence means `full`.

view.description: ECHO of the verbosity actually applied. ⚠️ Present ONLY when it differs from the default: a `full` response does not carry this field, and its absence reads as `full`. Check it before concluding anything from a missing block: in `standard` and `summary`, fields declared required on `Contrainte` are ABSENT because you declined them, never because the data is missing.

names.description: The submitted parameters this endpoint does not read (at most 20).

ParametresIgnores.description: Present in any response, at top level, as `ignoredParameters`, as soon as a query parameter is not read by the endpoint. ⚠️ The response is then NOT filtered by it: compare `names` with `accepted`.

truncated.description: ⚠️ True when the quota OR the server-side time budget was reached MID-BATCH (`truncatedReason` says which). The entries after the last returned index were NOT evaluated: do not read their absence as an absence of constraint.

items.description: A failed entry does not cancel the others: each element carries its own verdict, the same payload as `/substances/lookup` when `ok` is true, its own error otherwise.

truncated.description: ⚠️ True when the quota, the time budget (20 s) or the size budget (5 MB) was reached MID-BATCH (`truncatedReason` says which). The items after the last returned index were NOT evaluated: do not read their absence as an absence of data.

items.description: A failed item does not cancel the others. When `ok` is true, the item carries the same payload as `/substances/screening`.

truncated.description: ⚠️ True when the quota, the time budget (20 s) or the size budget (5 MB) was reached MID-BATCH (`truncatedReason` says which). The items after the last returned index were NOT evaluated: do not read their absence as an absence of data.

items.description: A failed item does not cancel the others. When `ok` is true, the item carries the same payload as `/substances/impurity-limits`.

truncated.description: ⚠️ True when the quota, the time budget (20 s) or the size budget (5 MB) was reached MID-BATCH (`truncatedReason` says which). The items after the last returned index were NOT evaluated: do not read their absence as an absence of data.

items.description: A failed item does not cancel the others. When `ok` is true, the item carries the same payload as `/substances/opinions`.

territory.description: The territory filter actually applied · `null` if none. ⚠️ An unknown query parameter is not applied (it is named in `ignoredParameters`): if you expected a code and read `null`, check the parameter NAME.

nextSince.description: The timestamp of the LAST row served. Kept for integrations that used it and to date a sync; it is NOT what you page with. ⚠️ Several hundred constraints can share one timestamp: resuming at that instant then returns the same page forever. Use `nextCursor`. Never advance it with your own clock: the gap with ours PERMANENTLY loses whatever was written in between. This bound is INCLUSIVE: deduplicate on (`logicalEntryId`, `knownSince`).

nextCursor.description: ⚠️ **The resume token · this is what you pass back as `cursor` on the next call**, after EVERY page, for as long as `truncated` is true. Opaque: store and return it verbatim, do not parse it. It carries the instant AND the row, so it crosses a batch written in a single microsecond and yields NO duplicates. `null` on an empty page · keep the cursor you already had.

caveats.description: What the `territory` filter does NOT carry in this feed: the feed serves only rows printed under that code, whereas `/substances/lookup` adds those of a directly applicable union or of a reference. The note names the territory to follow as well. Absent when there is nothing to say.

changeKind.description: ⚠️ `FIRST_RECORDED` says "new TO US", never "new IN LAW": an entry in force since 2012 that we read today for the first time carries this value.

event.description: `RECORDED`: a version as we recorded it, placed in the feed at its `knownSince`. `RETRACTION`: the notice that we WITHDREW this entry, placed at the instant of withdrawal · it reaches an incremental sync by `cursor` like any other news, even when the entry itself was received long before. Mark row `id` as withdrawn. On a full replay a withdrawn entry therefore appears twice (RECORDED with `changeKind: RETRACTED`, then RETRACTION): both say the same thing.

eventAt.description: The instant that places this row in the feed: `knownSince` for `RECORDED`, the instant of withdrawal for `RETRACTION` (ISO 8601, UTC).

changeDetection.description: What `changedFields` compares, and what it excludes: the knowledge window (which differs by construction) and the derived `rules` block (our reading, not the legislator's wording).

territory.description: The territory filter actually applied · `null` if none. ⚠️ An unknown query parameter is not applied (it is named in `ignoredParameters`): if you expected a code and read `null`, check the parameter NAME.

deadSourceUrls.description: ⚠️ Acts whose served `sourceUrl` no longer resolves. The CONTENT we serve for them is unchanged: what is broken is the link back to the official page. Do not read a dead link as a repeal, and do not cite it to an end user as a verifiable reference. The count spans the whole authorized scope, not the current page; a `403` or `412` is NOT included (the service refuses our robot, the page exists).

title.description: The title in the LANGUAGE of the legislator: a Mexican catalogue returns Spanish, a Korean one returns Korean. The reviewed English translation, where it exists, is in `titleEn`.

titleEn.description: The reviewed ENGLISH title, where one has been established. ⚠️ `null` means "not established yet", never "the text has no title": we do not manufacture a translation. Read `title` instead, always served in the legislator's language.

status.description: The DISPLAY state of the act (`IN_FORCE`, `SUPERSEDED`, `REPEALED`, `UPCOMING`, `DRAFT`…). ⚠️ A display field, NOT a computed one: the question "was this text applicable on such a date?" is answered from `validFrom` and `validUntil`, never from it. Together with `validUntil` it is what carries authority over the act's life · never `constraintCount`.

validFrom.description: The start of the period over which this act is held applicable, `YYYY-MM-DD`. Always served.

validUntil.description: The end bound, `YYYY-MM-DD`, when the act stopped applying. ⚠️ `null` reads as "no end RECORDED ON OUR SIDE", never "still in force, guaranteed": read `sourceUrl` and `/coverage` before concluding. A date here, on the other hand, is a positive finding · the act is bounded, do not cite it as current law.

supersededBy.description: The acts that REPLACED this one, oldest first. An EMPTY array when no repeal is recorded · never absent, so that nothing gets concluded from its absence. ⚠️ The real cardinality is 0 or 1, but nothing in the database enforces it: the day two acts declare themselves successors of the same text, we want to SEE it rather than suffer it. Capped at 5.

statusMeans.description: The sentence that says what this act's state lets you conclude, served on EVERY row · including when the act is alive, otherwise its absence would become a conclusion. Three shapes: the act is NO LONGER in force (it then points to `validUntil` and `supersededBy`), it is NOT YET in force (`validFrom`, `applicationDate`), or no repeal is recorded ON OUR SIDE · which is a statement about our corpus, not about the official gazette.

constraintCount.description: The number of constraints WE extracted from this text. ⚠️ A count NOT FILTERED by the act's validity: a REPEALED act whose annex has been mined can show hundreds of them while the act that repeals it shows ZERO, simply because its content has not been extracted yet. ⚠️ **NEVER pick the act to cite on this volume.** `status` and `validUntil` are what carry authority over the act's life, and `supersededBy` names its successor. A high count measures our extraction work, not the text's legal force.

territory.description: The territory filter actually applied · `null` if none. ⚠️ An unknown query parameter is not applied (it is named in `ignoredParameters`): if you expected a code and read `null`, check the parameter NAME.

withheldByScope.description: Content that EXISTS and matches the query, but whose source text may not be redistributed under this key's scope. This is a LICENCE limit, NEVER an absence of regulation. `count > 0` reads "there is something here, request access", and certainly not "nothing to report".

absenceMeans.description: ⚠️ THE field of this route. It says what an absence of results lets you conclude: NOTHING on an unextracted or partial coverage scope, "NOT AUTHORIZED" on a positive list, "not restricted by this coverage scope" otherwise.

extractedAt.description: When this scope was read (freshness of the coverage).

completeAsOf.description: The date on which this scope's EXHAUSTIVENESS was established · not to be confused with `extractedAt`, which says when the source was READ. Served only for a `COMPLETE` scope, because it is the date that anchors an actionable claim.

scopeIsOpenByItsOwnText.description: ⚠️ True when the scope declares ITSELF non-exhaustive, in its own text · two Chinese tables do (« prohibited components INCLUDE, BUT ARE NOT LIMITED TO, the substances in the table »). This is a property of the LAW, not of our extraction: do not wait for this scope to reach `COMPLETE`, it cannot.

x-relayx-scopes.read:public: The corpus. Serves texts whose redistribution right is `PUBLIC_DOMAIN` or `OFFICIAL_ACT`.
x-relayx-scopes.read:licensed: Adds `LICENSED` and `RESTRICTED` texts. CONTRACTUAL: not granted from the console. ⚠️ `UNQUALIFIED` (the default) is served to no one: until qualification has been done, an unestablished right counts as no right.

x-relayx-zones.description: Commercial ZONES are units of SALE, not legal realities. A subscription opens **EUROPE only** by default; each additional zone is contracted separately. A territory outside your zones returns NONE of its own rows, and `subscription.missingZones` names its zone · that is how you learn a market exists here without being in your contract. ⚠️ Exception: a member state of a union whose law applies there directly (France, zone `FRANCE`, under a `EUROPE` subscription) returns the union rows, under the union code, and the response carries a `territory` caveat saying the national layer is withheld.

x-relayx-mcp.description: Remote MCP (Model Context Protocol) server, served on the same host and authenticated with the SAME API key as the operations above. The scopes and zones served are those of the key. Each request consumes one unit of the SUBSCRIPTION quota, handshake included · that ceiling is the same one the HTTP operations draw on: there is no window per transport and none per key.

requiredHeaders.Accept: application/json, text/event-stream · ⚠️ BOTH types; the MCP specification requires them and the server returns 406 without them.

x-relayx-mcp.pagination: Every paginated MCP response carries a `pagination` block with `maxOffset` (the hard ceiling, served so it can be READ rather than guessed) and `offsetClamped`. ⚠️ When `offsetClamped` is `true`, the rows returned are those of the ceiling and NOT those of the requested offset, and `truncated` stays `true` forever: a "while truncated" loop then never ends and re-reads the same page. Check `offsetClamped` before looping again, then narrow the query (market, legislator, full identifier) or read the remainder through the HTTP API, whose `offset` parameter has NO ceiling at all.
x-relayx-mcp.authorization: OAuth 2.1 is NOT offered: authentication is by API key in a static header. Clients that require an OAuth flow (web connectors) therefore cannot connect; those that accept a header all can.
